name: interccom
description: One voice for all your Claude Code sessions: hear conclusions and questions, talk back hands-free.

tts_engine.title: Talking: speech engine
tts_engine.description: Who turns Claude's words into speech. Cloud: elevenlabs, deepgram, soniox, openai, cartesia. On your machine: local (a server with the OpenAI audio API, e.g. Kokoro-FastAPI) or command (a program, e.g. Piper).

stt_engine.title: Listening: speech engine
stt_engine.description: Who transcribes what you say. Cloud: elevenlabs, deepgram, soniox, openai, groq. On your machine: local (a server with the OpenAI audio API, e.g. Speaches/faster-whisper or whisper.cpp) or command (a program, e.g. whisper-cli).

listen_mode.title: Listening mode
listen_mode.description: always: everything you say is sent. wake: only speech starting with "hey Claude". off: no mic.

elevenlabs_api_key.title: ElevenLabs API key
elevenlabs_api_key.description: Needed only when ElevenLabs is chosen. The key needs both Text to Speech and Speech to Text. Falls back to ELEVENLABS_API_KEY.

deepgram_api_key.title: Deepgram API key
deepgram_api_key.description: Needed only when Deepgram is chosen for talking or listening. Falls back to DEEPGRAM_API_KEY. Get one at console.deepgram.com.

soniox_api_key.title: Soniox API key
soniox_api_key.description: Needed only when Soniox is chosen for talking or listening. Falls back to SONIOX_API_KEY. Get one at console.soniox.com.

openai_api_key.title: OpenAI API key
openai_api_key.description: Needed only when OpenAI is chosen for talking or listening. Falls back to OPENAI_API_KEY. Get one at platform.openai.com.

groq_api_key.title: Groq API key
groq_api_key.description: Needed only when Groq is chosen for talking or listening. Falls back to GROQ_API_KEY. Get one at console.groq.com.

cartesia_api_key.title: Cartesia API key
cartesia_api_key.description: Needed only when Cartesia is chosen for talking or listening. Falls back to CARTESIA_API_KEY. Get one at play.cartesia.ai.

tts_voice.title: Voice
tts_voice.description: A voice of the chosen talking engine (ElevenLabs voice ID, Soniox voice name, OpenAI voice, Cartesia voice ID, local server voice). Deepgram picks the voice with the model, e.g. aura-2-thalia-en. Blank: the engine's default.

tts_model.title: Talking model
tts_model.description: A model of the chosen talking engine, e.g. eleven_flash_v2_5, aura-2-thalia-en, tts-rt-v2, gpt-4o-mini-tts, sonic-3, kokoro. Blank: the engine's default.

stt_model.title: Listening model
stt_model.description: A model of the chosen listening engine, e.g. scribe_v1, nova-3, stt-async-v5, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, whisper-large-v3-turbo, Systran/faster-whisper-small. Blank: the engine's default.

stt_language.title: Speech language
stt_language.description: Language code for transcription (en, hr, ...), or auto to detect.

local_tts_url.title: Local TTS server URL
local_tts_url.description: For tts_engine local: base URL of your OpenAI-compatible speech server, ending in /v1 (Kokoro-FastAPI: http://127.0.0.1:8880/v1).

local_stt_url.title: Local STT server URL
local_stt_url.description: For stt_engine local: base URL of your OpenAI-compatible transcription server, ending in /v1 (Speaches: http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1).

tts_command.title: TTS command
tts_command.description: For tts_engine command. Text arrives on stdin; write audio to {out}. Example: piper --model C:\voices\en_US-amy-medium.onnx --output_file {out}

stt_command.title: STT command
stt_command.description: For stt_engine command. {in} is a 16 kHz WAV; print the transcript. Example: whisper-cli -m C:\models\ggml-base.en.bin -f {in} -nt -np

muted.title: Muted
muted.description: Keep the speak tool but play nothing.

autonomy.title: Coordinator autonomy
autonomy.description: What the coordinator may decide on its own. relay: only pass things on and ask you. routine: also answer routine questions. full: decide like a careful senior engineer. All three still ask about anything destructive or outward-facing.

autonomy_rules.title: Coordinator rules
autonomy_rules.description: Your own rules for the coordinator, in plain words, e.g. "never approve database migrations". The more restrictive rule wins.
